unit.title: Go-to-market, B2B and objectives
unit.description: GTM strategy, ICP, PLG versus SLG, ABM, demand generation and capture, dark funnel, north star metric, OKR, crossing the chasm

cards.definition: The description of the companies that get the most value from your product and are the most profitable to serve: sector, size, region, tech stack, triggers. A persona describes people; the ICP describes accounts.
cards.example: ICP: French logistics companies of 50 to 500 employees using Excel for planning and growing fast.

cards.definition: In B2B, several people decide together: user, manager, finance, IT, purchasing, sometimes legal. Content and sales must convince each of them with their own arguments.
cards.example: IT checks security, finance checks ROI, the users check ease of use.

cards.definition: Classifying launches by impact: tier 1 for big moves (new product, full campaign), tier 2 for notable features (blog, email, sales training), tier 3 for small updates (changelog).
cards.example: A new pricing model is tier 1; a new export format is tier 3.

exercises.prompt: What is the difference between an ICP and a persona?
choices: The ICP describes target companies, the persona describes people
They are two names for the very same thing
The persona is used only in B2B marketing
The ICP lists your current customers only
exercises.explain: In B2B you first choose accounts (ICP), then the people inside them (personas of the buying committee).

exercises.prompt: Users sign up for free, invite colleagues and upgrade as they use the tool. Which motion is it?
choices: Product-led growth
Sales-led growth
Account-based marketing
Outbound prospecting
exercises.explain: PLG lets the product drive acquisition and expansion. It suits tools with a fast time to value.

exercises.prompt: A software sold 200,000 euros a year to banks relies on account executives and long cycles. Which motion?
choices: Sales-led growth
Product-led growth
Viral growth
Self-serve only
exercises.explain: High price, complex buying committee and integration needs call for a sales-led motion, often with ABM.

exercises.prompt: You pick 30 target companies and build campaigns and content for each. What is it?
choices: Account-based marketing
Mass marketing
Programmatic buying
Affiliate marketing
exercises.explain: ABM treats each account as a market of one (or a few). Marketing and sales work the same list together.

exercises.prompt: A podcast and LinkedIn posts that teach your market without asking for anything: what is it?
choices: Demand generation
Demand capture
Lead scoring
Retargeting
exercises.explain: Demand generation creates future buyers. Search ads on solution keywords capture demand that already exists.

exercises.prompt: A prospect hears about you in a private Slack group, then types your name in Google: attribution will credit organic search.
exercises.explain: True. That is the dark funnel. Ask how did you hear about us on forms to see what tools cannot track.

exercises.prompt: Which is a good north star metric for a meal kit service?
choices: Number of meals delivered and cooked per week
Number of followers on Instagram
Number of visits to the homepage
Number of people in the marketing team
exercises.explain: A north star reflects the value customers get and predicts revenue. Vanity metrics do neither.

exercises.prompt: Which key result is well written?
choices: Trial to paid conversion from 8 to 12 percent by June
Do a lot more marketing during this quarter
Launch many campaigns on every channel
Become the best brand in our whole market
exercises.explain: A key result is measurable, with a baseline, a target and a date. The objective can be inspiring; the KR must be checkable.

exercises.prompt: Your tool is loved by early adopters but mainstream companies do not buy. What is this gap called?
choices: The chasm
The dark funnel
The long tail
The flywheel
exercises.explain: Geoffrey Moore: the early majority wants proof, references and a complete solution for one niche first.

exercises.prompt: A buying committee includes IT, finance and the end users. What should content do?
choices: Answer the specific concerns of each role
Speak only to the person who filled the form
Focus only on the lowest price
Avoid any technical detail
exercises.explain: IT wants security, finance wants ROI, users want simplicity. Missing one can kill the deal.

exercises.title: Launching a B2B tool in France
exercises.scenario: You launch a scheduling tool for home care agencies. 4,000 agencies in France, from 5 to 300 employees. Budget: 150,000 euros for year one.

choices: The ICP: which agencies gain most and pay best
The colour palette and the logo of the tool
The number of LinkedIn posts per week
The price of the enterprise plan only
steps.feedback: Every other choice (channels, messages, price, sales motion) depends on which accounts you serve first.

steps.prompt: Small agencies decide fast online; large networks need demos and IT checks. Which motion?
choices: Self-serve trial for small ones, sales-assisted for large ones
Only cold calls to every agency in France
Only a free plan, with no sales team
Only trade fairs, twice a year
steps.feedback: A hybrid motion matches the buying process of each segment.

steps.prompt: How do you set the yearly objective?
choices: One OKR: 120 paying agencies, with activation and churn as KRs
As many leads as possible, whatever the source
One million impressions on social media
A new feature shipped every week
steps.feedback: Tie the objective to customers and value, with measurable KRs, instead of activity or vanity metrics.

exercises.explain: ICP first, motion matched to how each segment buys, objectives tied to customer value.
